pr_title: Adding gh release download for .zip and .tar.gz
pr_body:
Fixes #2167

Adding ```gh release download``` support for fetching the default .zip or .tar.gz release files.

The user will be able to require the files by simply adding the ```--archive``` command line parameter.
```bash
gh release download v1.3.0 --archive=tgz
```

####
- [X] Implement basic functionality
- [x] Add stricter argument validations
- [x] Create tests

issue_context.title: `gh release download` is not working for .zip and .tar.gz release assets
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

For both github.com and enterprise github, I am unable to download the default .zip and .tar.gz release assets.
`gh --version`: gh version 1.1.0 (2020-10-06)

I first tried it on an enterprise private server and afterwards tried it on one of my own repositories.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. I have the following release: https://github.com/restechnica/taskforce/releases/tag/v0.0.2
2. I authenticated with `gh auth`
3. I run `gh release list`
4. I see the output 'v0.0.2  Latest  (v0.0.2)  about 1 month ago'
5. I run `gh release download v0.0.2`
6. I see the output 'no assets to download'

### Expected vs actual behavior

I expected the default .zip and .tar.gz release assets to be downloaded.
Instead I received the output 'no assets to download'.

### Logs

```
olivier@mbp taskforce % gh release list
v0.0.2  Latest  (v0.0.2)  about 1 month ago
olivier@mbp taskforce % gh release download v0.0.2
no assets to download
```
comments:
Thank you for reporting!

Unfortunately, right now the `release download` command doesn't work with the default `.zip` and `.tar.gz` assets, since they are not "real" assets in the sense that they were explicitly uploaded to a release. I understand, however, that the web UI always lists them among other assets and that people rely on the ability to download them, so we will add this functionality in a subsequent release. 👍

One use case for this is when building a package from source that has a large number of commits. Being able to download source at a specific release without having to pull a full repo with 10k+ commits would be nice. Of course this would need to be implemented in a way that doesn't break existing workflows that dont expect these extra files, so it can't be the default even when using the current syntax to download all files.
@myoung3 - you can do this already using [git directly](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-archive).
@james-lawrence  doesn't that depend on having already downloaded/cloned the entire repo?

> Of course this would need to be implemented in a way that doesn't break existing workflows that dont expect these extra files, so it can't be the default even when using the current syntax to download all files.

Agreed. And I think that you either need a zip or a tarball but not both. How about an extra flag like:
```
gh release download v1.2.3 --archive=zip
```
In this mode, only the built-in zip archive would get downloaded. Now the question is, should other assets also get downloaded if the release attaches any?
My inclination would be to design this as an either/or approach. If someone wants both the archives and the actual release files, executing two separate commands isn't particularly burdensome.

@myoung3 no it doesn't normally but apparently github doesn't allow the archive command (??? wtf github ;)), which I just surprisingly discovered myself. but bitbucket and gitlab do `git archive --remote="git@gitlab.freedesktop.org:pipewire/pipewire.git" --format=tar.gz -o archive.tar.gz master`
@mislav @myoung3 extra flag could do the trick. I would expect to only download the archive without other release files with that flag.
@mislav I cross paths with this issue again. Are there any plans to implement this? Would be great to download an archive in similar fashion as assets attached to a release.
@shiouen No plans from our side yet. This is marked `help wanted`; anyone is free to contribute!

> @shiouen No plans from our side yet. This is marked `help wanted`; anyone is free to contribute!

@mislav  I'll have a crack at it :)

review_comments: Why include `application/json` here? Does it change anything? If we didn't need it then the `downloadAsset` function doesn't need to accept an extra argument

During my tests with the actual API endpoint i would get an error from the server regarding the client not accepting the application/json in the ```Accept``` request header. No idea why actually.. have you seen it before @mislav ?
